stem: Choose the verb that completes the sentence in standard written English: “There ___ three spare keys in the drawer.”

choices.text: is
was
are
has

explanation: The grammatical subject after there is the plural phrase three spare keys, so are agrees. Is/was are singular; has does not form this existential construction.

stem: Complete the question in standard written English: “Did the courier ___ the parcel before noon?”

choices.text: delivered
delivering
deliver
delivers

explanation: Did carries the past tense, so the following main verb takes the base form deliver. Delivered duplicates the tense marking; delivering and delivers do not form the required question with did.

stem: Complete the account of a finished event yesterday: “At noon yesterday, Lira ___ the parcel to the porter.”

choices.text: hands
has handed
will hand
handed

explanation: Handed places the completed event at the specified past time. Present and future change the time; present perfect does not normally pair with a finished yesterday-time reference in this account.

stem: The caretaker locked the kitchen at 6:00. The porter arrived at 6:15 and could not enter. Which sentence preserves that sequence while making the earlier action explicit?

choices.text: When the porter arrived, the caretaker will lock the kitchen.
The caretaker had locked the kitchen before the porter arrived.
The caretaker locked the kitchen only after the porter arrived.
The caretaker has locked the kitchen before the porter arrives tomorrow.

explanation: Had locked marks an action completed before the past arrival. The alternatives move the locking to the future, reverse the sequence, or change the entire account to tomorrow.

stem: Intended meaning: only the folders with red tabs need scanning; other folders do not. Which sentence states this without treating the red-tab description as an aside about all folders?

choices.text: The folders, which have red tabs, need scanning.
All folders need scanning, including those with red tabs.
Only the folders that have red tabs need scanning.
The folders need scanning, although none has a red tab.

explanation: The restrictive that-clause identifies the required subset, and only limits the instruction to it. The comma clause describes the folders as a whole; all widens the instruction; none contradicts the stated group.

stem: Intended meaning: Tomas checked the list, but he did not correct or approve it. No claim is made about whether anyone else checked it. Which sentence best expresses that limit?

choices.text: Tomas only checked the list; he neither corrected nor approved it.
Only Tomas checked the list; he corrected and approved it.
Tomas checked only the list and approved it afterward.
Tomas did not check the list but approved it.

explanation: Only limits Tomas’s action to checking, and the second clause makes that scope explicit. Only Tomas instead excludes other checkers and adds forbidden actions; checked only the list restricts the object, not the work; the final alternative denies checking.

stem: Choose the revision that repairs both agreement errors while retaining the meaning: “The artist and the curator agrees that the labels beside each painting needs revision.”

choices.text: The artist and the curator agrees that the labels beside each painting need revision.
The artist and the curator agree that the labels beside each painting needs revision.
The artist and the curator agrees that the label beside each painting need revision.
The artist and the curator agree that the labels beside each painting need revision.

explanation: Artist and curator are two people, requiring agree. Labels is plural, requiring need; each painting occurs inside a modifying phrase and does not change that subject. The distractors repair only one error or introduce another.
